2.content: When evaluating a possible move, add a positive bonus proportional to the reduction in Manhattan distance to the goal compared to the current state. Larger distance reductions yield larger bonuses.

3.content: When rating moves, give a modest positive incentive to actions that break a recent back-and-forth pattern. If no safe distance-reducing moves exist, allow moves that increase Manhattan distance, and assign only a reduced penalty (instead of prohibitive) to risky moves that step onto a hole cell while still decreasing distance to the goal. This prevents loops and lets the agent consider risky progress-making moves when safe options would cause stagnation. Do not encourage trapping or back-and-forth oscillation patterns.
